newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa surges on chart-driven spec buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa surges on chart-driven spec buying.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended sharply higher on Thursday, bolstered by technically driven speculative buying amid a backround of longer-term supply concerns, traders said.
Benchmark September surged to a session high of $1,650, up $49, before scale-up trade selling and light profit-taking trimmed gains. September closed $38 a tonne higher, at $1,639.
Spot July jumped $44, to $1,595, while the back months finished up $38 to $45.

Cocoa prices headed higher at the opening, lifted by commission house buying, dealers said. Upward momentum accelerated after the September contract breached near-term resistance at $1,626-$1,628, touching off buy-stops.
"It took out stops, so it really was a technical rally," said one trader. "The specs are happy to buy it and there really are no sellers."
Traders noted a lack of selling by origin and said there was a perception that producers were generally well hedged.
Additionally, weakness in the U.S. dollar against the British pound also buoyed the market, as arbitrage bought less expensive dollar-denominated New York cocoa.

Although there were no fresh fundamentals in the market today, concerns of supply tightness in the coming crop year and talk of harvests being hit by dry weather in late 1997 from the El Nino continued to underpin prices.
"El Nino is in the backround and it does pose a real threat," said Refco Inc. analyst Ann Prendergast. "But the outcome is by no means conclusive at this stage and we still have plenty of stocks."
Technically, some traders continue to look for a downward correction and said that September may still take a stab at a chart gap between $1,540 and $1,516.
In the short-term, they pegged September support at $1,625, followed by stronger support at $1,596. On the upside, resistance was seen at September's life-of-contract high of $1,655, they said.

Traders await the bi-weekly Commitment of Traders report due after Friday's close. Sources are looking for a sharp increase in speculative long positions, which they said could make the market vunerable to a sell-off.
Volume was fairly heavy, at an estimated 14,129 lots.
